title: Projection vs Include
description: Learn when to use Select projection versus Include eager-loading in EF Core, and how each choice affects query performance and data transfer.

data.text: EF Core gives you two main ways to bring related data into your query results: `Include` for eager-loading full entity graphs, and `Select` projection for pulling only the columns you need. Choosing between them is one of the most impactful performance decisions you can make.

`Include` tells EF Core to load related entities as part of the same SQL query using a JOIN. It is convenient because EF Core automatically reconstructs the object graph for you — navigation properties are populated without extra queries. However, Include loads entire related rows, even if you only need one or two columns from the related table.

data.title: Using Include to eager-load related data
data.code:
var orders = await dbContext.Orders
    .Include(o => o.Customer)
    .Include(o => o.OrderItems)
        .ThenInclude(oi => oi.Product)
    .Where(o => o.OrderDate.Year == 2025)
    .ToListAsync();

data.text: `Select` projection lets you specify exactly which columns to fetch. Instead of loading full entities, you shape the result into a lightweight DTO or anonymous type. Because EF Core only queries the columns you list, the SQL is leaner and the data transfer is smaller. This is especially valuable for API responses where you do not need the full entity.

data.title: Projecting into a DTO

items.title: Include
items.description: Eager-loads full related entities. Best when you need the complete entity graph for updates or when passing entities to the UI.
pros: EF Core tracks all loaded entities automatically
Simple to write for simple object graphs
cons: Loads all columns from related tables
Can produce large JOIN result sets
Risk of cartesian explosion with multiple collections

items.title: Projection (Select)
items.description: Fetches only the columns you specify. Best for read-only API responses, reports, and list views.
pros: Minimal data transfer from the database
No change-tracking overhead for projected types
Avoids cartesian explosion on collection includes

data.title: Cartesian explosion warning
data.text: Including multiple collection navigations (for example, Orders with OrderItems and Payments) in a single query multiplies the row count. A single order with 5 items and 2 payments produces 10 database rows. Projection is usually the safer choice for list endpoints.

items: Use projection for API responses, list views, and reporting where you only need a subset of columns.
Use Include when you need full entities for editing or when the object graph is shallow.
Prefer explicit loading for optional related data that is only needed in some code paths.
Combine projection with filtered Include when you need the entity tracked but only a subset of its children.

data.title: Filtered Include
data.code:
var orders = await dbContext.Orders
    .Include(o => o.OrderItems.Where(oi => oi.Quantity > 1))
    .Where(o => o.Id == orderId)
    .FirstOrDefaultAsync();

data.title: Key takeaways
items: Projection fetches only what you need and avoids tracking overhead.
Include is convenient but can fetch unnecessary columns and cause cartesian explosion.
For read-only API responses, project into DTOs rather than returning tracked entities.
Use filtered Include when you need tracked entities with limited related collections.
